title: Building an alumni network that supports your school
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on building a genuine alumni network — one that provides mentorship, resources, and a positive reputation loop for the school.
body:
Most Kenyan schools lose touch with their graduates almost entirely the moment they leave. This represents a significant missed opportunity — alumni who maintain a connection to their former school can provide mentorship for current students, contribute resources, enhance the school's reputation, and offer a source of institutional pride that benefits current students' sense of belonging.

Start capturing alumni contact information systematically

The most basic and most commonly missed step is simply maintaining contact details for graduating students. A brief exit form during Grade 12's final weeks — capturing email, phone number, and intended next step — creates the foundation for an alumni network that most schools currently lack entirely.

Create a reason for alumni to stay connected

Alumni who are only contacted when the school wants a financial contribution quickly disengage. A relationship that offers genuine value in both directions — the school sharing updates alumni find interesting, inviting them to relevant events, celebrating their achievements — builds a connection that alumni want to maintain, which in turn makes them far more willing to contribute when asked.

Low-cost starting point: A simple WhatsApp broadcast list or Facebook group for alumni, updated with school news, achievements, and occasional opportunities to engage, requires minimal resources but creates a genuine ongoing connection point.

Alumni as mentors and career guidance resources

Recent alumni are often the most relatable and credible source of career guidance for current students, particularly Grade 12 students navigating post-school decisions. A structured programme inviting alumni back to speak about their university, TVET, or career experience — even informally over a school holiday — gives current students access to genuinely relevant, recent experience.

Alumni as a resource for school development

Successful alumni sometimes have professional skills, networks, or resources that can directly benefit the school — a former student now working in construction who can advise on a facility project, an alumnus in a relevant industry who can arrange student attachments or donate equipment. These connections rarely materialise without a deliberate effort to maintain the relationship in the years after graduation.

Building alumni pride through shared identity

Schools with strong alumni cultures typically have some shared identity elements — an alumni association name, an annual gathering, recognition of notable alumni achievements shared with current students. These elements, even modest ones, build the sense of ongoing belonging that keeps alumni engaged over the long term.

Starting small and building over time

An alumni network does not need to launch fully formed. Starting with basic contact capture, a simple communication channel, and one modest annual touchpoint — even just a holiday season message — builds the foundation that can grow into a more structured programme over several years, as the alumni base and the school's engagement with it both mature.
